fixes.explanation: Hilkiah the priest finds the Book of the Law of the LORD while the money is being brought out. Somebody went in to carry money out and came out holding Scripture. That's the best surprise anybody has ever found during repair work, friend. Everything after this hangs on that book.

This verse never mentions the ark. What Hilkiah the priest finds is the Book of the Law of the LORD. I get why the ark came to mind when someone finds a treasure in the temple. Hold on to the book, baker, because the rest of the story is about it.

Joshua was Moses' assistant (Joshua 1:1), so he's in the right neighborhood. Still, the verse says the book was given by Moses. Moses is the name on this one, and Joshua is one more name to keep straight. Next time you see this one, think Moses.

That's right. Shaphan the scribe tells the king the money found in the house of the LORD has been paid out and put into the hands of the supervisors and workers. He says the servants are doing all that has been placed in their hands (2 Chronicles 34:16). Good report, baker, and then he gets to the book.

That's true. After he tells the king that Hilkiah has given him a book, Shaphan reads it in the presence of the king. So Josiah doesn't just hear about the book. He hears it read right there in front of him.

When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his clothes. Later the LORD says Josiah's heart was tender, and that he humbled himself, tore his clothes and wept before Him (2 Chronicles 34:27). I think those words hit him hard, baker.

Josiah tells them, “Go and inquire of the LORD for me…” That's concerning the words in the book that has been found. He sends the men to ask the LORD about it, which tells you how seriously the king takes what he just heard.

Josiah never orders copies in this passage. His order is to go and inquire of the LORD concerning the words in the book that has been found. Copies for every city would be a big project, baker, and the text doesn't mention one. The order is to inquire of the LORD.

No hiding happens here. Josiah has just heard the book read, and he sends five men to inquire of the LORD about it. Later he reads it aloud to all the people (2 Chronicles 34:30). That book is about as far from hidden as a book can get, friend.

No crowning happens in this passage. Josiah goes up to the house of the LORD with all the people, great and small, and reads all the words of the Book of the Covenant in their hearing. If a crowd that big gathers, I'd guess it's for something big, and the text says it's the book. The only thing on the program is the reading, friend.
